summary_paragraph: A woman with multiple comorbidities, including morbid obesity, COPD, obstructive sleep apnea, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, atrial fibrillation, and type 2 diabetes, was admitted after being found somnolent and confused at her nursing home. She presented with altered mental status, hypoxia, hypotension, and acute kidney injury. Evaluation revealed hypercapnia and respiratory acidosis likely due to missed oxygen therapy and COPD exacerbation, contributing to encephalopathy. Her hypotension resolved with IV fluids, and her kidney function normalized. She was continuing outpatient ertapenem for a recent ESBL E. coli urinary tract infection; antibiotics were temporarily switched to meropenem during admission. Her mental status improved with oxygen support and hydration. The diuretic dose was reduced due to hypotension, and home medications were optimized. She was discharged to extended care with plans to complete IV antibiotics, follow up on anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation, and improve adherence to oxygen and CPAP therapy.
